headline: Lancashire firm diverts 25M LEGO bricks from landfill
meta_description: A Lancashire company has kept 25 million LEGO bricks out of landfill while making pre-owned sets 40–60% cheaper for families.
summary_short: A Lancashire company has saved 25 million LEGO bricks from landfill while offering pre-owned sets at 40–60% discounts.
body:
A Lancashire company has saved 25 million LEGO bricks from landfill while making pre-owned sets available at 40–60% below retail price.

The initiative tackles two problems at once: reducing plastic waste and making the beloved building blocks affordable for more families. By reselling and refurbishing LEGO sets that might otherwise have ended up in landfills, the company extends the lifespan of plastic that can last for decades.

The scale of the operation speaks to both the volume of LEGO entering waste streams and the growing appetite for sustainable alternatives to buying new. Each brick saved is one fewer piece destined for disposal—and families gain access to creative play at a fraction of the cost.
quick_facts: 25 million LEGO bricks diverted from landfill
Pre-owned LEGO sets sold at 40–60% discount
